skill.name: orca-cli
skill.description: Resolve the Orca CLI for the current session and retrieve its version-matched guide before managing Orca resources.
skill.summary: Discover the correct Orca executable, load its CLI guide, and handle common startup and compatibility errors.
skill.author: zpyoung

security_audit.summary: All 18 static alerts are false positives: Markdown delimiters are not shell execution, and shell names only describe compatibility. One semantic concern remains: sandbox denial triggers an unconditional instruction to rerun with escalated permissions. No evidence found of malicious prompt injection or data exfiltration; the runtime guide and executable implementation are outside this audit.

remediation.issue: Sandbox denial automatically triggers a request for expanded execution permissions.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval and platform authorization before escalation, preserve enforced sandbox restrictions, and stop if permission is unavailable.

content.user_title: Discover and Use the Correct Orca CLI
content.value_statement: Different Orca installations can expose different executables and commands. This skill selects the session executable and retrieves its version-matched guide before further operations.
actual_capabilities: Selects the session executable using Orca environment variables and platform-specific fallback rules.
Avoids the GNOME Orca screen reader when selecting a Linux CLI outside managed terminals.
Retrieves the version-matched orca-cli guide from the selected executable.
Recommends structured JSON output and command help for further discovery.
Defines startup recovery, executable failure handling, and read-only fallback when guide retrieval is unsupported.
limitations: Requires an installed Orca executable that the current session can access.
This package contains a discovery stub, not the full operational guide or executable implementation.
Worktree, terminal, browser, and automation operations depend on the runtime guide and installed Orca version.
Sandbox restrictions can prevent runtime access; permission changes require user approval and platform authorization.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Development Session
use_cases.description: Select the correct executable and retrieve its guide before planning Orca worktree operations.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Agent Handoff
use_cases.description: Load the installed guide to discover supported terminal and worktree commands before coordinating another agent.

use_cases.title: Diagnose CLI Compatibility
use_cases.description: Investigate executable failures, Linux naming conflicts, and missing guide commands without switching silently to another build.

prompt_templates.title: Discover the CLI
prompt_templates.prompt: Identify the Orca CLI for this session and retrieve its version-matched guide. Report failures without switching executables.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Supported Commands
prompt_templates.prompt: Load the Orca guide and identify supported read-only worktree discovery commands. Use help where needed and avoid changing state.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an Agent Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Using the loaded Orca guide, plan a handoff to another agent in a worktree. Request confirmation before creating resources or sending terminal input.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Runtime Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose Orca startup or runtime access failures using the selected executable. Stop at sandbox denial and request authorization before any permission escalation.

output_examples.input: Which Orca executable should I use on Linux outside an Orca-managed terminal?
output_examples.output: Use orca-ide unless the session environment selects another executable. Avoid bare orca because it may launch the GNOME screen reader.

output_examples.input: What should happen when the selected executable cannot run?
output_examples.output: Report the exact error and stop. Do not switch to another executable because it may target a different Orca build.

output_examples.input: My Orca installation does not recognize the guide retrieval command.
output_examples.output: Updating Orca restores guide retrieval according to the skill. Until then, use command help for read-only discovery and avoid guessing unsupported commands.

best_practices: Resolve one trusted executable and reuse it throughout the session.
Load the version-matched guide before operations and prefer structured JSON output.
Obtain user approval and platform authorization before permission escalation or state-changing actions.
anti_patterns: Running bare orca on Linux outside managed terminals without checking executable selection.
Switching silently to another executable after a failure or guessing unsupported commands.
Treating sandbox denial as authorization to bypass restrictions.

faq.question: Does this package contain the complete Orca command guide?
faq.answer: No. It retrieves the version-matched guide from the selected Orca executable.

faq.question: How does the skill select an executable?
faq.answer: It prioritizes ORCA_CLI_COMMAND, then a development session, then the Linux-specific fallback, and finally orca.

faq.question: Why should Linux users avoid bare orca outside managed terminals?
faq.answer: That name can resolve to the GNOME screen reader. The skill selects orca-ide in that context unless an earlier selection rule applies.

faq.question: Can it help with worktrees and agent handoffs?
faq.answer: It loads guidance intended for those workflows. Exact supported operations depend on the installed Orca version and retrieved guide.

faq.question: What happens if guide retrieval is unsupported?
faq.answer: The skill recommends updating Orca and using command help only for read-only discovery until guide retrieval is available.

faq.question: Should runtime access denial trigger automatic escalation?
faq.answer: No. The skill suggests escalation, but user approval and platform authorization are required before expanding access.
